videos.title: The Ultimate Guide to Elemental Craft

order: Find the ore before anything else. Guide's literal opening instruction: 'The first thing you want to find is the inert crystal.' elementalcraft:inert_crystal_ore / elementalcraft:deepslate_inert_crystal_ore -> elementalcraft:inert_crystal. Guide calls it 'one of the first two things you need in the mod'.

The other of those first two things is a source of element. Elements are drawn from world sources (elementalcraft:source) via elementalcraft:elementpipe into a holder - nothing works without a live element supply.
First machine is the elementalcraft:infuser. Guide spends its whole early section on it: 'you've just clicked on the element infuser... the infuser will put the stone in with the earth element'.

Pipes are a three-step ladder the guide calls out explicitly: 'The book talks about three levels, broken, normal and improved' -> elementalcraft:elementpipe_impaired -> elementalcraft:elementpipe -> elementalcraft:elementpipe_improved.

Infusion produces the mod's basic materials: elementalcraft:drenched_iron_ingot (water infusion on iron) and elementalcraft:burnt_glass (fire infusion on glass) are the two first-tier outputs, confirmed in the jar's recipe files.
Then binding, which is the tier above infusion and needs far more element: elementalcraft:swift_alloy_ingot (air, 1250) then elementalcraft:fireite_ingot (fire, 30000).

The elementalcraft:pureinfuser is the mid/late gate and is a MULTIBLOCK. Guide: 'the pure infuser, which technically is a multiblock' - it needs all four elementalcraft:pedestal_fire, elementalcraft:pedestal_water, elementalcraft:pedestal_earth, elementalcraft:pedestal_air around it, and each pedestal is itself a 30000-element binding recipe.
elementalcraft:purecrystal comes out of the pure infuser and unlocks the last tier of machines: elementalcraft:purifier and elementalcraft:spell_book.

Shrines (elementalcraft:shrinebase + elementalcraft:groveshrine, elementalcraft:oreshrine, elementalcraft:lavashrine, elementalcraft:growthshrine ...) plus elementalcraft:shrine_upgrade_capacity and the rest of the upgrade family are the automation layer and come after the machine chain works.
gates: The whole machine tree is gated by three crystal grades, and this is visible in the jar's own unlock conditions rather than in any video: elementalcraft:contained_crystal unlocks elementalcraft:infuser, elementalcraft:binder and elementalcraft:extractor; elementalcraft:strongly_contained_crystal unlocks elementalcraft:crystallizer and elementalcraft:pureinfuser; elementalcraft:purecrystal unlocks elementalcraft:purifier and elementalcraft:spell_book.

Every binding and infusion recipe carries an element_type AND an element_amount, so a recipe is gated on having the RIGHT element in sufficient quantity, not just the ingredients. elementalcraft:fireite_ingot needs 30000 fire; elementalcraft:groveshrine needs only 2500 water.
The pure infuser cannot run without all four elemental pedestals built, which makes it a four-element gate rather than a single-element one.

Gem quality is a three-step gate on tools and jewels: elementalcraft:crude_fire_gem -> elementalcraft:fine_fire_gem -> elementalcraft:pristine_fire_gem (and the same for earth, water, air). The guide mentions choosing 'fine, pristine, crude' when following a scroll recipe.
elementalcraft:spell_book and elementalcraft:staff sit behind purecrystal, so the mod's magic-facing content is late, not early.
mechanics: Four elements - fire, water, earth, air - are a FLUID, not an item. They are gathered from world sources, piped, stored in elementalcraft:element_holder_fire / _water / _earth / _air and elementalcraft:reservoir_fire / elementalcraft:reservoir_water / elementalcraft:reservoir_earth / elementalcraft:reservoir_air, and spent by recipes. This is the mod's whole identity and no item-chain quest captures it.

Two recipe verbs: infusion (one input item + one element type, cheap) and binding (several inputs + one element type, expensive). elementalcraft:pureinfuser adds a third that consumes all four at once.

Sources can be farmed rather than found: elementalcraft:natural_air_source_seed / elementalcraft:artificial_air_source_seed (and the other three elements) plus elementalcraft:source_breeder mean element supply is a production problem.
elementalcraft:rune + elementalcraft:minor_rune_slate / elementalcraft:major_rune_slate are the global modifier system - runes buff the machines rather than the player.
elementalcraft:inscriber, elementalcraft:spell_desk, elementalcraft:scroll and elementalcraft:jewel / elementalcraft:unset_jewel form the gear-customisation side.
elementalcraft:purerock and elementalcraft:whiterock are the mod's building stone, produced by the same machines - a lot of jar ids are decorative variants and should not be mistaken for progression.
traps: Do not treat the many *shrine_upgrade_* ids as progression steps - there are ~25 of them and they are sidegrades chosen per shrine.
Do not build quests around the ~40 whiterock/purerock slab/stair/wall ids; they are decoration and inflate the id count.

The guide is a dubbed translation and mangles nearly every proper noun ('Murni' for pure, 'eye' for gem). Item names taken from that audio alone are unreliable - everything in these notes was checked against elementalcraft-1.20.1-6.0.1.jar.
